zotero.abstractNote: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has achieved remarkable success in representation learning. However, most state-of-the-art methods rely on large batch sizes or memory banks to store representations, which can be computationally expensive and memory-intensive. In this work, we propose a memory-efficient parametric instance discrimination approach that avoids the need for large batch sizes or memory banks. Our method, which we call Occam's Razor for SSL, learns a parametric model of the data distribution, allowing for efficient instance discrimination. We demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance on standard benchmarks while significantly reducing memory requirements.
